title: Restriction identities for prefix deletion
statement: Let I be linearly ordered, p≥0, n=p+2, t:Fin(n)→I, and let O,N be the outgoing/incoming filtered subtypes described by stable sorting and partial sorting [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators]: O consists of (σ,a,τ,r) with σ,τ permutations of Fin(n), a:Fin(n), r:Fin(n+1), σ stable for t, τ partial sorted with prefix a, and r<a. N consists of (j,ρ,b,η) with j:Fin(n), ρ,η permutations of Fin(n-1), b:Fin(n-1), ρ stable for t∘j.succAbove, η partial sorted with prefix b, and (t(j),j) strictly preceding (t(j.succAbove(ρ(b))),j.succAbove(ρ(b))) lexicographically. For any equivalence e:O≃N satisfying a=b+1, r<n and τ(r)=j for every e(σ,a,τ,r)=(j,ρ,b,η), the following hold for every such x and every k:Fin(n-1): σ(r.succAbove(k))=j.succAbove(ρ(k)) and τ(r.succAbove(k))=j.succAbove(η(k)). The two restrictions follow from the base facts and uniqueness of stable and partial sorting, without using any particular construction of e.

proof.text: Fix x and use its base facts a=b+1 and tau(r)=j. Prefix agreement, since r<a, gives sigma(r)=j. For each permutation pi with pi(r)=j, construct a permutation of Fin(p+1) by composing finSuccAboveEquiv r, the subtype equivalence induced by pi between the complements of r and j, and the inverse of finSuccAboveEquiv j. Its defining equation is pi(r.succAbove k)=j.succAbove(restriction k). The private proved helper restrict_perm verifies this equation directly from apply_symm_apply.

The private proved helper stable_restrict transfers monotonicity and the equal-value tie condition through the strictly increasing successor embeddings. Mathlib Tuple.eq_sort_iff identifies this stable restricted permutation with the incoming rho.

Construct the restricted tau in the same manner. For k<b, the successor position is below a=b+1, hence prefix agreement and the already proved restriction equation for sigma identify its prefix with rho. For b<=k<l, r<a and a=b+1 force a<=r.succAbove(k); strict monotonicity of r.succAbove and the increasing tail of tau give the increasing tail of the restriction, reflected through j.succAbove. Apply cechPartialSort_existsUnique to identify the restriction with incoming eta, and substitute both equalities into the defining restriction equations. All inequalities are finite-index arithmetic; p=0, b=0, b=p and repeated tuple values are included.

theorem prefixDeletionRestrictions {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (p : ℕ)
    (t : Fin (p + 2) → I)
    (e : ({x : Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 2)) × Fin (p + 2) ×
      Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 2)) × Fin (p + 3) //
    (cechStableSort t x.1 ∧ cechPartialSort x.1 x.2.2.1 x.2.1) ∧
      x.2.2.2.val < x.2.1.val}) ≃
      ({y : Fin (p + 2) × Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1)) × Fin (p + 1) ×
      Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1)) //
    (cechStableSort (t ∘ y.1.succAbove) y.2.1 ∧
      cechPartialSort y.2.1 y.2.2.2 y.2.2.1) ∧
    (t y.1 < t (y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)) ∨
      (t y.1 = t (y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)) ∧
        y.1 < y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)))}))
    (h : ∀ x, let y := e x
      x.1.2.1.val = y.1.2.2.1.val + 1 ∧
      ∃ hr : x.1.2.2.2.val < p + 2,
        x.1.2.2.1 ⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ = y.1.1) :
    ∀ x,
      let y := e x
      ∃ hr : x.1.2.2.2.val < p + 2,
        (∀ k : Fin (p + 1),
          x.1.1 ((⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ : Fin (p + 2)).succAbove k) =
            y.1.1.succAbove (y.1.2.1 k)) ∧
        (∀ k : Fin (p + 1),
          x.1.2.2.1 ((⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ : Fin (p + 2)).succAbove k) =
            y.1.1.succAbove (y.1.2.2.2 k))
